loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_intro:
Reinforcement learning policy spaces are high-dimensional objects whose geometry is poorly understood. Category-theoretic invariants---drawn from iquantum group representation theory and algebraic structures studied by Lab-Epsilon---may characterise which policy classes are equivalent under symmetry transformations, yielding provable convergence or robustness guarantees.

This is the most theoretically demanding proposal in the collaboration: only Epsilon's algebra work and, tangentially, Gamma's systematic KGE review are directly relevant. Alpha's voice-RL results, Beta's competitive offline RL, and Delta's sim-to-real transfer work are adjacent but not core to the category-theoretic framing.

The 5Q proposal must be precise about scope: it should define which policy-space invariants are targeted, what algebraic machinery is imported, and what empirical grounding is planned. Citing a peripheral unpublished result as 'supporting evidence' without clear relevance should be challenged during the collaboration.

This task is the hardest in the pilot: five PIs, only a few on-topic results, and a narrow theoretical framing that requires careful citation-relevance judgement.
loader_kwargs.proposal_topic_title: Category-Theoretic Invariants of Multi-Agent RL Policy Spaces
